subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw adopt automatic per-sender Feishu group subagents with isolated skills/config/memory, or keep the current session/thread isolation model and require a narrower plugin/API design first?
rationale: The source shows adjacent session and thread-binding mechanisms, but the requested automatic group subagent lifecycle crosses product, security, resource-management, and plugin/core boundary choices that cannot be inferred from existing behavior.

options.title: Design first
options.body: Keep this open for maintainer design of the Feishu/channel subagent lifecycle, authorization, quota, memory, and skill/config policy before implementation.

options.title: Limit to session isolation
options.body: Declare `groupSessionScope` plus explicit bindings/subagent spawns as the supported model and move any remaining per-user assistant workflow into narrower follow-up items.

options.title: Prototype as plugin experiment
options.body: Ask for an external Feishu/channel plugin experiment that proves the lifecycle and security model before changing core or bundled plugin contracts.

recommendation.title: Design first
recommendation.body: Keep this open for maintainer design of the Feishu/channel subagent lifecycle, authorization, quota, memory, and skill/config policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin metadata names this handle as community maintainer and the issue timeline already routes Feishu-related attention there.
